svg.text: talk.01 · v0.2 study · THREE FRONTS, KEY ON THE LEFT, WHEEL ON THE RIGHT
the walkie / TE convention for the key (upper left) · our own wheel in the top-right corner · three ways to lay out the face
TENTATIVE · NOT A FINAL DESIGN
front views at 10 mm = 45 px · the key may stick out 5 mm, the wheel about 1 mm
F1 STRIP
a colour strip down the side you touch · skin SAND
· Reads as a Walkman / pocket radio, not as TE's top-and-
bottom split.
· The colour strip is also the colour of the key: the part
you touch is the loud part.
· Risk: the tall slots sit close to the key; keep the key's
5 mm clear of the grille.
F2 WINDOW
a dark inset window and a rainbow band · skin POPPY
· Closest to a vintage radio: the speaker window is the
hero.
· The rainbow band gives a horizontal, TE-like stripe
without copying its layout.
· Risk: the three bands start to look like TE's two tiers
again if the window is too wide.
F3 CIRCLES
one motif: the circle, big and small · skin SAND
· The wheel is a small circle and the grille a big one: the
repeated motif.
· The dot disc is the easiest grille to print and to read as
a microphone.
· Risk: the most 'designed', so the most to get right; the
disc must not look like a camera lens.
Same on all three: the key on the left, upper half (y 12 to 58 mm), slanted, 5 mm out at most; the wheel in the top-right chamfer with its rim about 1 mm out;
four mode pictograms printed on the face (DICT, TALK, OPEN, LOCK); the coiled cable and USB-C on top; the back is the earlier small hatch and small U stand.
